c9f59605-9d45-4507-8dd6-f9b4e38ca6fa.title: Charli XCX will join Madonna on ‘Danceteria’ remix
c9f59605-9d45-4507-8dd6-f9b4e38ca6fa.incipit: Madonna and Charli XCX are teaming up for a remixed version of Madonna’s hit Danceteria. The song, which recounts how Madonna got her start in the music industry after persuading DJ Mark Kamins to play her...
c9f59605-9d45-4507-8dd6-f9b4e38ca6fa.body: Madonna and Charli XCX are teaming up for a remixed version of Madonna’s hit Danceteria . The song, which recounts how Madonna got her start in the music industry after persuading DJ Mark Kamins to play her demo tape in a nightclub, has become one of the most popular tracks on her Confessions II album. - Advertisement - Fans have been calling for additional remixes of the song, and Madonna has now revealed that the Afterhours Mix , featuring Charli XCX, will be released on 24 September. So far, the only official reworking of the track has been a remix by DJ Harry Romero. he collaboration was announced in a social media video featuring Madonna repeatedly saying her name and Charli XCX’s. The short clip rapidly cuts between images of both artists dancing. “You wanna talk about Madonna and Charli?” the singer asks before a brief snippet of the new version of the song is played. In the clip, Madonna wears a red hoodie featuring a photograph of herself from the 1980s. Madonna previously teamed up with Sabrina Carpenter for the single Bring Your Love, while Kylie Minogue appeared a reworked version of Love Sensation. Soon, the Madonna will take to the stage at the MTV Video Music Awards, where she has reportedly received 11 nominations. It marks the first time Madonna has led the MTV Video Music Award nominations since 1998, when she released Ray of Light . She also led the nominations in 1990 following the success of Vogue . On both occasions, she received nine nominations, making this year’s total a career best. The VMAs will take place on 27 September in Los Angeles, and there is considerable anticipation surrounding Madonna’s appearance. She has delivered several memorable moments at the awards over the years, including rolling across the stage in a wedding dress at the inaugural ceremony in 1985 and sharing a headline-making kiss with Britney Spears and Christina Aguilera.

4e8546c7-7a66-4f17-b1de-e535876dde46.title: Miley Nearly Hits No. 1 On Her First Visit To A Chart She’s Never Seen Before
4e8546c7-7a66-4f17-b1de-e535876dde46.incipit: It's been less than two years since Billboard inaugurated its Hot Dance/Pop Songs chart, a ranking of the most popular tracks that straddle the line between those two styles. For years, pop stars would invade...
4e8546c7-7a66-4f17-b1de-e535876dde46.body: It's been less than two years since Billboard inaugurated its Hot Dance/Pop Songs chart , a ranking of the most popular tracks that straddle the line between those two styles. For years, pop stars would invade the dance and electronic rankings with massive wins, including stars like Lady Gaga, Beyoncé, Rihanna and more. Then the electronic-leaning tallies began embracing more obscure artists, while the more dance-focused cuts from superstars couldn't find the same footing on pop tallies. Billboard also does not publish some of the same style rosters in the pop field as it does in other genres, as there is no list for pop tunes on streaming sites or general consumption. There is no Hot Pop Songs rundown these days. Miley reaches the Hot Dance/Pop Songs register for the first time and nearly conquers it on her inaugural visit with the first taste of a newly released album. Miley Nearly Rules the Hot Dance/Pop Songs Chart "Bass Persuades" almost rules the Hot Dance/Pop Songs chart as it arrives. The cut – the first single from the newly-released album of the same name – opens at No. 2, bringing Miley into the top 10 and almost to the peak position on her inaugural trip to the tally. Zara Larsson Blocks Miley From No. 1 Miley is blocked from the peak position by Zara Larsson. Her smash "Midnight Sun" is steady at No. 1 for a milestone tenth frame. It is only the fourth track to rule Billboard 's Hot Dance/Pop Songs chart for that length of time. "Bass Persuades" Leads This Week's Debuts The Hot Dance/Pop Songs chart features only 15 spaces, and three of them are occupied by debuts. Miley collects the loftiest of the bunch this time around. Newcomer Adela starts her tune "Boys" at No. 8. Blackpink member Jisoo lands in the lowest rung at No. 15 with a solo tune titled "Click." Miley Debuts Her New Single at No. 2 on Two Charts "Bass Persuades" does not open at No. 1 on any Billboard roster, but it does sit at No. 2 on a pair of them. In addition to the Hot Dance/Pop Songs chart, Miley's latest single comes in second place on the Digital Song Sales tally. On that roster, it trails Ella Langley's "Choosin' Texas," which earns a seventeenth stint at No. 1. As "Choosin' Texas" reaches that figure, it matches with "Despacito" by Daddy Yankee, Luis Fonsi and Justin Bieber as the third-longest-running ruler ever. "Bass Persuades" Debuts on Nine Billboard Rankings "Bass Persuades" launches on nine Billboard charts this week, and it's a top 40 hit almost everywhere. The track misses that region on both the Streaming Songs roster and Billboard Global Excl. U.S., but otherwise becomes a quick winner. Miley's latest opens inside the top 10 on three rankings, including its No. 3 start on the Dance Streaming Songs list. Miley Almost Debuts Her Album At No. 1, But An R&B Star Keeps Her At Bay This article was originally published on Forbes.com

307fa99b-7480-42d7-a298-3d653a34361a.title: Exclusive: Steven Sater Gave Update on Musical NERO With Duncan Sheik 2 Weeks Before His Death
307fa99b-7480-42d7-a298-3d653a34361a.incipit: Duncan Sheik’s frequent collaborator Steven Sater spoke highly about their musical Nero, which is scheduled to open this fall in London, less than three weeks before the songwriter died at age 56. “I’m so...
307fa99b-7480-42d7-a298-3d653a34361a.body: Duncan Sheik ’s frequent collaborator Steven Sater spoke highly about their musical Nero , which is scheduled to open this fall in London, less than three weeks before the songwriter died at age 56 . “I’m so excited about Nero ,” Sater exclusively told BroadwayWorld in an interview that took place on August 31. “We had been working on Nero for so long. The last proper workshop we had done was with Lea Michele , Idina Menzel and Michael Arden in 2009, and it was thrilling.” Andrew Barth Feldman is slated to star in the new musical from the Tony Award-winning Spring Awakening creators about Roman emperor Nero. It features a book and lyrics by Sater with music by Sheik. Sheik, who rose to fame with the 1996 pop song “Barely Breathing” before becoming a force in the musical theater landscape, was working on new projects up until his untimely death on September 17. He died of heart failure leading to cardiac arrest, per People . When it came to Nero , Sater explained, “We spent the past couple of years developing this in London, and it’s been brilliant. It could not be more timely, I’ll say that. And the fact that it’s opening right before the midterms — if indeed we have midterms — is kind of remarkable.” The musical, Sater said, is “really about this thwarted theater kid who wants to just be a star, and his mom pushes him into the seat of power, and he’s like, ‘Okay, I’ll try playing emperor.’” “It’s hugely Shakespearean,” Sater explained, adding that the musical has “epic themes” and all this “dirty, scandalous, outrageous stuff of ancient Rome.” The songs, he said, are “totally on brand for Duncan and me, but they’re different — there’s a waltz, there’s a samba, there’s a tango.” Sater and Sheik won a Tony Award for Best Original Score of Spring Awakening , for which Sheik was also awarded Best Orchestrations. The groundbreaking rock musical, featuring haunting songs about self-discovery and teen angst, also won the Tony for Best Musical. Lindsay Posner is directing Nero , with choreography by James Cousins . “We’re launching it in this theater called Southwark Elephant,” said Sater. “It’s sort of like going back to the Atlantic, for me.” When asked if the creative team thinks Nero may cross the pond and play in New York City, Sater told BroadwayWorld, “I hope so. I think someone could do it here. It’s only seven actors and ensemble.” After all, added Sater, “I’m the guy who always believed that Spring Awakening could succeed on Broadway.” Sheik’s other new musical Memoirs of Amorous Gentlemen , an adaptation of Moyoco Anno’s manga, is scheduled to begin performances at The Night Egg at Culture Club in Chelsea on September 25, in a new production from Rob Ashford . An Off-Broadway revival of Sater and Sheik’s groundbreaking musical Spring Awakening , directed by Tony Award winner Danya Taymor with choreography by Celia Rowlson-Hall , is scheduled to open this fall . Spring Awakening is also celebrating the original Broadway cast recording being released by Decca Broadway next month on vinyl . “Listening to this album is so transporting for me ,” Sater told BroadwayWorld. bf937cbb-6fc2-4796-bfb3-2096c8795293.title: “I always had to think, ‘Is Brent gonna like this?’ Pretty soon, he didn’t like anything that we would come up with”: Bill Kelliher on his difficult songwriting sessions with Brent Hinds
bf937cbb-6fc2-4796-bfb3-2096c8795293.incipit: (Image credit: Gary Miller/Getty Images) Bill Kelliher has looked back on his songwriting partnership with the late Brent Hinds, which he says felt like a “competition”.Hinds’ exit from Mastodon in March...
bf937cbb-6fc2-4796-bfb3-2096c8795293.body: (Image credit: Gary Miller/Getty Images) Bill Kelliher has looked back on his songwriting partnership with the late Brent Hinds , which he says felt like a “competition”. Hinds’ exit from Mastodon in March last year sent shockwaves through the fanbase. His tragic death several months did the same. The band has since released their first record following his death, Marrow Deep. Speaking in the new issue of Guitarist , guitarist and key songwriter Kelliher admits writing with Hinds was a rocky experience. “I’m constantly writing. With Brent, it was always a competition, which I didn’t understand. It was one-sided with him,” he says. “He was interesting – a great fucking guitar player and songwriter – but it was difficult to write with him. With this new stuff, I’m writing all the time and putting riffs into my phone. “But with Brent, after a while, he was just on his own wave... He just wasn’t into it any more. I was like, ‘Dude, how great is it that we get to go up on stage, have people buy our albums and worship you?’ But he just had this self-destructive streak.” The band said they were unsure about speaking out about Hinds’ troubles, and the manner in which they reluctantly parted ways, given that he wasn’t around to contribute to the conversation. Still, Hinds’ legacy lacquers Marrow Deep – a record they see as a tribute as well as a fresh start. Sadly, something had to change. “We were on totally different ends of the spectrum as far as guitar and personality,” Kelliher continues. “We did have a lot of things in common, but he was dangerous. I think that’s what made the Mastodon we were in the early days. He would just do whatever the fuck he wanted to do, but that got old after a while.” All the latest guitar news, interviews, lessons, reviews, deals and more, direct to your inbox! (Image credit: Joby Sessions/Future) After a relentless career that’s produced nine albums and six Grammy nominations, the band is an established institution. At 55, Kelliher is the oldest of the core group, and everything the guitarist says points towards them growing up, while Hinds was stuck in a destructive place. It’s hard to hear, but he says life in the band improved when he left. “Honestly, it was like a big weight had been lifted,” Kelliher confesses of Hinds' departure from the band. “I was doing the lion’s share of the writing, but I always had to think, ‘Is Brent gonna like this?’ And pretty soon, he didn’t like anything that we would come up with.” Hinds once said he hated heavy metal – a soundbite that went on to make many headlines. But that only scratched the surface of the effervescent and complex personality he was. Mastodon - Snakes For Dinner (Official Video) - YouTube Watch On Now the band is facing a lawsuit from the late guitarist’s estate, claiming they financially benefited from his image following his death. The band has strongly refuted the claims. They’ve also added another member to their live lineup, Baroness’ John Baizely. He’ll join them on their US tour with Deafheaven and Alcest. Kelliher’s full interview features in the new issue of Guitarist . You can pick up print and digital copies from Magazines Direct . A freelance writer with a penchant for music that gets weird, Phil is a regular contributor to Prog , Guitar World , and Total Guitar magazines and is especially keen on shining a light on unknown artists. Outside of the journalism realm, you can find him writing angular riffs in progressive metal band, Prognosis , in which he slings an 8-string Strandberg Boden Original, churning that low string through a variety of tunings. He's also a published author and is currently penning his debut novel which chucks fantasy, mythology and humanity into a great big melting pot.

bf96d245-42b8-4458-aab0-68fbfad6ddd4.title: Miley Cyrus Ends a 13-Year Wait for a Billboard 200 No. 1 With ‘Bass Persuades’
bf96d245-42b8-4458-aab0-68fbfad6ddd4.incipit: Bass Persuades debuts at No. 1 on the Billboard 200, giving Miley her first chart-topping album since Bangerz in 2013 Physical sales drove the launch, backed by a large spread of vinyl, CD, download, and cassette variants Riley Green and beabadoobee both earned their first top 10 albums in a week shape
bf96d245-42b8-4458-aab0-68fbfad6ddd4.body: Bass Persuades debuts at No. 1 on the Billboard 200, giving Miley her first chart-topping album since Bangerz in 2013 Physical sales drove the launch, backed by a large spread of vinyl, CD, download, and cassette variants Riley Green and beabadoobee both earned their first top 10 albums in a week shaped by new arrivals Miley Cyrus , now billed simply as Miley, is back at the top of the Billboard 200 for the first time in more than a decade as Bass Persuades debuts at No. 1 on the chart dated October 3. The album earned 61,000 equivalent album units in the US during the week ending September 24, per Luminate. It gives Miley her sixth No. 1 and her 16th top 10 album overall. Traditional album sales made up 47,000 of the album’s units, enough to top the Top Album Sales chart as well, while SEA units added 14,000, the equivalent of 14.22 million on-demand official streams. TEA units contributed only a negligible amount. The sales figure got a clear boost from the variety of formats on offer: 16 vinyl variants and nine CD versions, each with one edition carrying a bonus track, plus six download editions (most with bonus material) and a cassette. The rollout moved quickly. Miley announced Bass Persuades on September 1 and shared its title track as the lead single two days later. That song entered the Billboard Hot 100 at No. 35 on the chart dated September 19, becoming her 24th top 40 hit. The album arrived on September 18, only a little over a year after Something Beautiful , which debuted and peaked at No. 4 on the Billboard 200 dated June 14, 2025. Her previous chart-topper came in October 2013 with Bangerz . Her tally of six No. 1s and 16 top 10s spans releases billed as both Miley and Miley Cyrus, and it also counts her soundtrack albums recorded as Disney’s Hannah Montana. The long gap puts Miley in company that keeps growing this year. She’s the third act in 2026 to return to No. 1 after waiting at least a decade. Bruno Mars got there first on the March 14 chart, debuting The Romantic 13 years after Unorthodox Jukebox last took the top spot in March 2013. A$AP Rocky followed with Don’t Be Dumb , which opened at No. 1 on the chart dated January 31, just over 10 and a half years after At.Long.Last.A$AP led the list in June 2015. The race for the top spot was close. Ella Langley ‘s former No. 1 Dandelion holds at No. 2 with nearly 61,000 units, up 1%. Right behind her, Riley Green earns his first top 10 as That’s Just Me debuts at No. 3 with 60,000 units, his biggest week yet. His launch leaned more evenly on streaming. Album sales accounted for 29,000 units, a career best that ranks No. 2 on Top Album Sales. SEA units added 30,000, equal to 30.89 million on-demand official streams and good for a No. 10 start on Top Streaming Albums. TEA units contributed 1,000. On the physical side, Green offered 13 vinyl and CD variants, some with bonus tracks, along with two download editions (one with a bonus track) and a cassette. Three former No. 1s come next. Morgan Wallen ‘s I’m the Problem stays at No. 4 with 58,000 units, up 1%. Olivia Rodrigo ‘s you seem pretty sad for a girl so in love slips from No. 3 to No. 5 with 55,000 units, down 8%. Noah Kahan ‘s The Great Divide falls one spot to No. 6 with 46,000 units, up less than 1%. beabadoobee also reaches the top 10 for the first time as Pylon opens at No. 7 with 35,000 units, her best week by that measure. Sales made up 25,000 of those units, another personal best, placing the album at No. 3 on Top Album Sales. SEA units added 10,000, equal to 10.79 million on-demand official streams, while TEA units were negligible. Her format lineup included 10 vinyl variants and three CDs, with signed editions in both, plus two cassettes and a download. The bottom of the top 10 features one steep drop. Jhené Aiko ‘s Westside Whimsy falls from No. 1 to No. 8 in its second week with 35,000 units, down 53%. Drake ‘s former leader ICEMAN slides from No. 6 to No. 9 with nearly 35,000 units, down 2%. Kahan’s Stick Season holds at No. 10 with 34,000 units, up 3%, giving him two albums in the top 10.

801236f3-2f9f-4c43-a342-a25497e67dfd.title: The only member of Led Zeppelin to earn Ginger Baker's respect
801236f3-2f9f-4c43-a342-a25497e67dfd.incipit: Despite having barely been together for three years, Cream managed to make the most of that brief window and ensured that they carved...
801236f3-2f9f-4c43-a342-a25497e67dfd.body: Despite having barely been together for three years, Cream managed to make the most of that brief window and ensured that they carved themselves a legacy and became one of the most celebrated rock bands of an era. Their instant impression had a reasonable amount to do with the fact that their three members were already highly regarded musicians in their own right. Bassist and vocalist Jack Bruce had previously enjoyed stints with Blues Incorporated and the Graham Bond Organisation, both alongside future Cream drummer Ginger Baker, while he’d also been alongside former Yardbirds guitarist Eric Clapton as part of John Mayall and the Bluesbreakers. Because all parties had amassed rather impressive résumés prior to joining forces, what they were bound to make as a trio would already have had potential listeners salivating at the prospect, and they didn’t disappoint with what they ended up delivering. On top of the fact that these three much-lauded musicians were collaborating on the same project, what they were doing was entirely new as well, with the band seemingly ushering in what would go on to be seen as hard rock. Yes, it featured elements of the blues rock that they’d all dealt in the past, but it also served as a precursor of sorts to heavy metal, and therefore became a major influence to so many other bands who would emerge in the years immediately after them. During a 1997 interview published by Forbes , Baker was asked about how he felt Cream had influenced others, and while he was willing to acknowledge that they’d helped to create an entire movement, he was less enthusiastic about praising any of the musicians who had taken a considerable amount of inspiration from Cream’s work. “Jimmy’s a good player,” he appeared to reluctantly say about Led Zeppelin’s Jimmy Page, acknowledging that he was one of the few devotees of Cream whose work he actually admired. However, Baker wasn’t quite certain that Led Zeppelin were anywhere near as good as the band he’d previously been a part of , and that Page was arguably the only part of the band that he had any interest in, despite the fact that they probably boasted one of the greatest drummers of all time in John Bonham. “I don’t think Led Zeppelin filled the void that Cream left, but they made a lot of money,” he proposed, evidently unimpressed with their pastiche of what he, Bruce, and Clapton had made. “I probably like about 5% of what they did; a couple of things were really cool. What I don’t like is the heavy bish-bash, jing-bap, jing-bash bullshit.” Of course, Page and Clapton were more than familiar with each other due to their involvement in the Yardbirds, albeit at different times, and so the influence of Clapton would always have been there for Page. However, as for Baker’s comments on whether Led Zeppelin were any good on the whole, perhaps it comes with a slight bitterness that they were able to survive longer and gain the success that he believed Cream were owed . Cream arguably did the legwork in making the style of music a viable option, and Led Zeppelin took that to stratospheric levels. b67a1ea9-c41c-40fa-a165-35ebf5c12ea5.title: ‘JAŸ-Z in 8’: 11 Things We Learned From Episodes 1–3
b67a1ea9-c41c-40fa-a165-35ebf5c12ea5.incipit: JAŸ-Z, Rick Rubin HBO One of Jay-Z‘s biggest selling points as a rapper has been...
b67a1ea9-c41c-40fa-a165-35ebf5c12ea5.body: JAŸ-Z, Rick Rubin HBO One of Jay-Z ‘s biggest selling points as a rapper has been the depth of his storytelling and lyricism. Over 30 years into his career, fans are still breaking down his bars and uncovering meanings. Hov has decided to participate in this ongoing activity, sitting down with Rick Rubin for his new eight-episode documentary JAŸ-Z in 8 . A special screening of the documentary was held on Sept. 13 at the Metropolitan Opera Museum in New York City. It began with a red carpet, where celebrities such as Jermaine Dupri , DJ Khaled , Fat Joe , Skylar Diggins and Neil deGrasse Tyson strutted their stuff and spoke to the media. The Roc Nation leader himself even pulled up, taking the time out to speak with nearly every single outlet that was present. “Nothing was difficult,” he told Billboard exclusively when asked if there was anything hard to reflect on while putting the documentary together. “It wasn’t difficult at all. It was easy. The ease of the conversation with Rick [Rubin]; he’s super curious about life [and] music. We share the same love for music. It was an easy conversation.” As for the screening, attendees got to witness Jigga Man dive deep into records such as “You Must Love Me,” “4:44,” “This Can’t Be Life” and “What More Can I Say.” Through the conversations, he unveiled some thoughts that many people may not have heard before, and Billboard has the gems. Here are 11 key takeaways from the first three episodes, from Jay-Z’s least-played songs and the pressure that fuels his creativity to his thoughts on The Notorious B.I.G., Tupac Shakur, streaming, and the criticisms of his own work. Why He Doesn’t Take “Stealing Lines” Claims Seriously Obviously, he rapped about this on “What More Can I Say,” and his thoughts were as clear as day. He’d use a Biggie line to uplift the late wordsmith and Brooklyn, where they are both from. However, he broadened his thoughts to hip-hop as a whole and said the genre was built on paying homage. Whether it’s flipping lines, mimicking flows, or sampling, Hov believes countless people who have called themselves rappers are inspired by those before them and pay their respects in creative ways, which isn’t wrong. Especially when, like him, his signature style is so lauded and generational. Tupac’s Supposed Weaknesses Are Actually Strengths The father of three and Rubin went on a tangent at one point, and the late Tupac Shakur came up in conversation. The “Allure” rapper enthusiastically explained that while there are narratives about Pac not being the best technical rapper, his strengths actually lay in how raw and authentic his delivery was. He was able to take concepts so simple, such as “Dear Mama,” and turn them into timeless anthems. Jay said rap was often graded on a criterion of complexity, but in reality the most “basic” things are what can really get the job done. There was a clear affinity for the West Coast legend’s artistry. One (Album) and Done The “Can’t Knock the Hustle” spitter’s past as a, well, hustler has been long-documented. He spoke to Rubin about how rappers were initially viewed as corny or lame by those who pushed drugs in the streets and made a comfortable living off of that. Initially, that was his primary occupation, and rap was something he did not plan to make a career out of, so much so that he originally only planned to put out one album. Obviously, that changed when he took off the way he did in the late ’90s, but just imagine an alternate universe where Jay-Z’s discography was solely made up of Reasonable Doubt . “Black Album” Had “So Many Obvious Misses” Jay is often a very boastful individual in and out of his music, so people haven’t heard him acknowledge errors too often unless he is getting very personal in his raps. However, in this documentary, he revealed some missteps from his 2003 “retirement” LP, The Black Album . First, he felt that “Encore” should have been the lead single instead of the popular “Change Clothes.” He admitted they almost took “Encore” to radio, but there was a difference of opinion between himself and former Def Jam President Kevin Liles. Additionally, Hov believed that “What More Can I Say” would’ve been a more powerful project closer than “My 1st Song.” The Advantage of Streaming With the “Encore” regret in mind, Jay spoke about how “picking” the single doesn’t necessarily exist anymore. Artists can simply put the album out, fans gravitate toward a song, and there’s the possibility of a record with no hook going No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100. Obviously many artists still do release promotional singles and select songs that go to radio, otherwise known as “focus tracks” but sometimes the cut that takes off is completely unexpected. Beyond that, he felt streaming cut the red tape and allowed hip-hop to push past the gatekeepers. The genre was highly popular, but the accessibility opened the door for it to be the legitimate biggest genre in the world. “Brooklyn’s Finest” Expanded His Artistry The production of this record followed a standard four-beat structure, but both Hov and Biggie ended up having five bars each measure thus they would’ve sounded off beat if the track was left as is. Jay had to write in some “connectors” to help Biggie know when he should come in on the song to keep it orderly and sounding right. He spoke about how prior to this he had no real experience writing hooks, as Reasonable Doubt featured other people handling them or the very simple “Can I Live.” He also edited some of Big Poppa’s verse, removing the “Who shot ya” line to not spark more tension with Tupac and the West Coast. So, in the end, working with Big on “Brooklyn’s Finest” prompted him to take a new approach to ensure the song would be its best. The Notorious B.I.G and Tupac Beef From his perspective, the legendary rappers were close friends. Biggie told Pac did not trust some people in Pac’s circle as he was blowing up. The “California Love” artist told those men about Big’s apprehension toward them, which caused friction. He even avoided going into a club with Hov and Ty Ty because those men were present. Nonetheless, Pac blamed Biggie for him being shot in NYC, instead of the unreliable people in his vicinity. Of course, the rest of their dissolved relationship is history, but also lead to their unfortunate demises. Jigga stated that he didn’t even like going to the West Coast for a long time because of their beef. What Triggers the Storytelling Part of His Artistry Hov has rapped over all types of beats and instruments from some of the best producers to ever grace music. Some of his best records are when he invites people into his psyche and takes them on a trip into his past. He revealed that hearing string instruments is what prompts him to want to deliver a narrative-like record to listeners. It might be time for a “Best Jay-Z String Songs” list. The Most Conscious Thing He Ever Heard It is always fun to hear rappers give superlatives to their catalogs. For Jay, the award for “The Most Conscious Thing He Ever Heard” goes to the hook on “This Can’t Be Life” with Beanie Sigel and Scarfare from 2000’s The Dynasty: Roc La Familia compilation album. “This can’t be life, this can’t be love/ This can’t be right, there’s gotta be more, this can’t be us,” he says twice in the chorus. Once again, it is so simple, but he dedicated a lot of time to the mindset he had in this track and the layered meanings. When you factor in the in-depth verses from all three lyricists, it is hard to argue with him. “I Run to the Pressure” Jay-Z’s recent residency at Yankee Stadium and his overseas shows have proven one thing: he still loves performing and takes it very seriously. However, one revelation from the documentary may have shocked people: he only starts relearning lyrics and committing them to memory about a week before he is set to hit the stage. With such a vast catalog and the possibility of performing something on a whim, this may sound crazy. For the 25-time Grammy winner, though, it fuels him. “I run to the pressure,” he told Rubin. This may be one of his most impressive feats, and that says a lot given his resume. Jay-Z’s Least Played Songs There were two moments in the screening where he was visibly less enthused: discussing “You Must Love Me” and “4:44.” The former, a 1997 record, details his remorse for how he acted toward his mother as a child, shooting his brother, and how he treated an ex-girlfriend who assisted him in drug transactions. The latter, 20 years later, was dedicated to his wife, Beyoncé, whom he had been unfaithful to. The 56-year-old artist admitted that these are his least-played songs in his discography simply because they are hard to hear and reflect on. He was open about his transgressions and appreciated that he was in a state of mind to convey these thoughts, but it was the most vulnerable version of him that was shown in the screening. 41439c39-c9b4-4551-831f-ca380b716b2a.title: Ed Sheeran set for solo show: Showtime pushed later amid Macklemore controversy
41439c39-c9b4-4551-831f-ca380b716b2a.incipit: The Ed Sheeran concert in Philadelphia is set to begin later than its original performance time after his support acts dropped out in support...
41439c39-c9b4-4551-831f-ca380b716b2a.body: The Ed Sheeran concert in Philadelphia is set to begin later than its original performance time after his support acts dropped out in support of Macklemore, who was axed from the lineup after calling for a free Palestine. All eyes have been on the forthcoming concert at Lincoln Financial Field slated for September 19th, as earlier this week Macklemore was fired from Sheeran’s Loop Tour for expressing solidarity with Palestine. Macklemore explained that Robert Kraft, the owner of the Patriots and Gillette Stadium in Foxborough, told Sheeran that he had “rallied some of the other stadium owners ” and gave him the “ultimatum” that the tour would not go ahead if the rapper performed. Sheeran released his own statement on the matter, insisting, “I am not complicit. I have my personal views on this devastating conflict.” However, all of Sheeran’s other support acts, namely Finneas, Aaron Rowe, and Lukas Graham, as well as his backing band Beoga, withdrew from their planned appearances . As a result, the concert is now scheduled for 8pm, pushed on from the previously advertised 5:30pm start. As per FOX 29 Philadelphia , stadium parking lots are scheduled to open at 3pm and doors are now at 6pm, as Sheeran gears up to take the show solo. Additionally, local station 6abc also reported that the show would proceed without support acts. Meanwhile, pro-Palestinian protest group Shutdown DZ Philly has also called supporters to head down to the stadium at around 4:30pm local time to protest the event. In the midst of all this, resale prices have fallen while the stadium appears far from sold out only hours from kick-off. At the time of writing, fans are still waiting for official word from Sheeran. Sheeran’s former support acts, BIIRD and Myles Smith, also recently distanced themselves from the ‘Castle on the Hill’ singer for his handling of the situation. 19563d31-8932-4c54-b9dd-5a508a7adea0.title: 5 Things You Missed From Night 1 Of The 2026 iHeartRadio Music Festival
19563d31-8932-4c54-b9dd-5a508a7adea0.incipit: Kenny Chesney's set was just the beginning of an incredible night. BTS, Cardi B, Goo Goo Dolls, Weezer, and Zara Larsson all shut down the stage last night with show-stopping performances...
19563d31-8932-4c54-b9dd-5a508a7adea0.body: Kenny Chesney's set was just the beginning of an incredible night. BTS , Cardi B , Goo Goo Dolls , Weezer , and Zara Larsson all shut down the stage last night with show-stopping performances you won't see anywhere else. Scroll below to see more of the biggest moments you might've missed. Don't forget to tune in tonight for the second act featuring performances by Benson Boone , Ciara , Lainey Wilson , LE SSERAFIM , Major Lazer , Muse , Snoop Dogg , The Smashing Pumpkins , and Stella Lefty . Cardi B stuns in zebra-print outfit while performing all her hits Cardi B understood the assignment when she pulled up to the iHeartRadio Music Festival stage in a sparkling zebra bodysuit with red fringe. Bardi put on a red-hot performance as she belted out massive hits like "WAP," "Bodak Yellow," "Up," and her latest single "AH HA." She rocked the stage solo while delivering fan favorites like "Finesse," "I Like It," "Taki Taki," and "ErrTime." The crowd went wild as she brought the drama by performing songs like "Hello," and "Pretty & Petty." She even held it down for her fans in the Caribbean with a memorable performance of "Bodega Baddie." Weezer brings out surprise guest Remi Wolf during their set Weezer had a surprise in store for fans in Las Vegas. The “Island in the Sun” band — which consists of Scott Shriner, Rivers Cuomo, Patrick Wilson, and Brian Bell — transported the crowd back to the 90s and 2000s with their career-spanning set. During their performance, the group surprised fans with singer-songwriter Remi Wolf, who joined the band for “Go Away.” The guys even gave BTS a shout-out after performing songs like “Beverly Hills,” “Undone (The Sweater Song),” and “Buddy Holly." “I’m excited to see BTS!" Rivers Cuomo exclaimed. "Weezer loves you!” Zara Larsson brings a lucky fan on stage to do the "Lush Life" dance with her Zara Larsson had one of the most vibrant sets of the night. After bringing hits like "Midnight Sun," "Pretty Ugly" and "Blue Moon" to life, Larsson invited one excited fan up on stage to do the viral "Lush Life" dance with her while performing the fan-favorite song. The sweet moment has become a tradition at her shows, with lucky concert-goers getting to show off their moves alongside the singer in what she has said is her "favorite part of the show." Goo Goo Dolls lead fans in a singalong of "Iris" The Goo Goo Dolls have plenty of hits under their belts, but there's one that continues to pull at heartstrings to this day. During their set at the iHeartRadio Music Festival, the seasoned band led the fans in a singalong of their biggest hit, "Iris," that echoed throughout the T-Mobile Arena. It was a moment that fans will remember forever. BTS closes out the show with their biggest hits BTS closed out the first night with an unforgettable set. The group — consisting of RM, Jin, Suga, J-Hope, Jimin, V and Jungkook — kicked off their performance with "SWIM," the lead single from their latest album ARIRANG . The group continued with a dynamic performance of "2.0," and later shouted out their supporters before singing their fan favorite "MIC Drop." They wrapped up their set with a high-energy rendition of "FYA" as bursts of flames lit up the stage.
